remaining_subclaims.subclaim: The Goliad massacre occurred after Mexicos declaration for the execution of Texian rebels.
remaining_subclaims.rationale: According to the documents, the Mexican Congress passed a decree on December 30, 1835, stating that armed foreigners taken in combat were to be treated as pirates and executed. This decree was the basis for the execution of the Texian prisoners at Goliad. Therefore, the Goliad massacre did indeed occur after Mexicos declaration for the execution of Texian rebels.

remaining_subclaims.subclaim: Dillard Cooper was a survivor of the Goliad massacre.
remaining_subclaims.rationale: According to the provided documents, Dillard Cooper was indeed a survivor of the Goliad massacre. He was one of the four members of Shackelfords Red Rovers who escaped after days on the run. Coopers account of the massacre and his survival is mentioned in the documents.

remaining_subclaims.subclaim: Dillard Cooper met other survivors of the Red Rovers.
remaining_subclaims.rationale: After surviving the Goliad massacre, Cooper linked up with three other surviving members of Red Rovers, Zachariah S. Brooks, Wilson Simpson, and Isaac D. Hamilton.

remaining_subclaims.subclaim: The Goliad massacre involved the execution of Texian rebels.
remaining_subclaims.rationale: The documents state that the Goliad massacre involved the execution of 425-445 Texian prisoners of war by the Mexican Army, under the orders of General Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna, on March 27, 1836.

remaining_subclaims.subclaim: The Red Rovers had survivors who met Dillard Cooper.
remaining_subclaims.rationale: According to the documents, Dillard Cooper was a member of the Red Rovers and survived the Goliad massacre. He linked up with three other surviving members of the Red Rovers, Zachariah S. Brooks, Wilson Simpson, and Isaac D. Hamilton, after the massacre.
